title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability, function/tool calls, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Asha Mehta
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity improvements: streaming stability fixes, function/tool calling parity with structured output, support for roles and stop/logprobs parameters, and consistent response formatting. No breaking changes.
description: Context: We need parity with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions for customers migrating existing integrations. This PR closes ENG-1245 and targets streaming stability, function/tool calls (structured output and tool selection), roles handling, stop/logprobs support, and response formatting. Work done: - Implemented compatibility layer for new/legacy params (role tokens, message arrays) - Streaming: made chunk framing deterministic, added backpressure metrics, improved reconnection logic to avoid truncated events - Function/tool calling: added support for tools schema in model responses, JSON-first parsing, and structured output enforcement via schema validation - stop/logprobs: implemented stop sequence handling and logprob passthrough where supported by model backend - Response formatting: normalized 'choices' shape to match OpenAI shape (index, message.content delta, finish_reason), added 'usage' breakdown. Checklist: - [x] API compatibility for roles and messages - [x] Streaming stability (timeouts, chunk merging) - [x] Function/tool call wire format + schema validation - [x] stop sequences and logprobs support - [x] SDK integration tests updated - [x] E2E canary with hosted runtime Changes are backward-compatible for our existing API but enable OpenAI-compatible params. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration notes and examples.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add chat.completions parity layer and request param mappings
fix(streaming): deterministic chunk framing and reconnection backoff
feat(functions): support tool schema in model responses and structured output validation
feat(params): add stop and logprobs passthrough and server-side enforcement
test(e2e): add openai-compat integration tests and canary config
chore(docs): update openai_compat docs with examples and migration guide
review_comments: Miguel Torres: LGTM overall, but we need explicit tests for multi-tool responses and tie-breaker behavior when multiple tools match.

Elena Park: Streaming improvements look good; request to add a metric for 'streaming.chunk_merge_count' and alert if chunk loss > 0.1%.
Asha Mehta: Added metric and alert to observability/metrics_streaming.md and wired into canary config.
Samir Patel: Please ensure logprob exposure is gated behind a feature flag for certain model backends (we don't want sensitive logits by default).

ci_checks_summary: Unit tests: pass (runtime, api, sdk python/ts)
E2E canary: pass (deployed to staging cluster)
Benchmarks: perf regressions within threshold (<2% token latency)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge by Elena Park on 2026-02-20. Commit message consolidated feature and fix commits. Post-merge: rollout to staging via canary (tests green) and scheduled rollout to prod in 48h.
notes: Migration notes: - SDKs: Python and TypeScript wrappers expose openai_compat mode via Client(openai_compat=True). - Customers using stop sequences should test with canary; some older model backends do not support logprobs passthrough. - No change to existing Redwood API behavior unless openai_compat flag turned on.
